name: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy type V
aliases: distal spinal muscular atrophy type V

clinicalPearls: Autosomal dominant distal motor neuropathy notable for early and prominent involvement of the hands, particularly wasting of the thenar and first dorsal interosseous muscles
Caused by variants in GARS (glycyl-tRNA synthetase) or BSCL2 (seipin), the same genes that can produce overlapping distal and upper-limb-predominant phenotypes
Presents with distal upper-limb weakness and wasting, sometimes preceding or exceeding lower-limb involvement, with foot deformity developing later
Sensory examination and sensory nerve studies are essentially normal, defining it as a pure motor (distal spinal muscular atrophy) disorder rather than a sensorimotor CMT
GARS variants can cause a spectrum spanning dHMN-V and axonal CMT type 2D, illustrating shared molecular pathways
Electrophysiology shows reduced motor amplitudes with preserved conduction velocities and normal sensory responses, reflecting motor axonal loss
Diagnosis requires the distal, upper-limb-predominant motor pattern together with genetic confirmation
reference.pathophysiology: Distal hereditary motor neuropathy type V is a dominantly inherited motor axonopathy caused by variants in genes such as GARS, which encodes glycyl-tRNA synthetase, and BSCL2, which encodes seipin. Glycyl-tRNA synthetase is required for protein translation and appears to have additional roles in the axon; pathogenic variants are thought to exert a toxic effect that preferentially damages the longest and most metabolically demanding motor axons, especially those supplying intrinsic hand muscles. Seipin variants cause endoplasmic reticulum stress in motor neurones. The pathology is confined to motor axons, so sensory function and conduction velocities are preserved while motor amplitudes fall.
additionalDifferentials: Other distal hereditary motor neuropathy subtypes
Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis with distal hand wasting
Multifocal motor neuropathy with conduction block
Inclusion body myopathy or other distal myopathies
additionalInvestigations: Nerve conduction studies and electromyography showing motor axonal loss with normal sensory responses
GARS and BSCL2 sequencing or a distal hereditary motor neuropathy panel
Anti-ganglioside antibodies and conduction-block studies to exclude multifocal motor neuropathy
Cervical MRI where a focal cause of hand wasting is suspected
Creatine kinase and muscle imaging to exclude distal myopathy
redFlags: Rapidly progressive or asymmetric weakness suggesting motor neurone disease
Conduction block indicating potentially treatable multifocal motor neuropathy
Sensory loss, which should prompt reconsideration of the pure motor diagnosis
reference.prognosis: Typically slowly progressive with disability largely confined to distal limb function; ambulation is usually preserved and life expectancy is normal.
pitfalls: Missing treatable multifocal motor neuropathy, which can mimic distal motor neuropathy
Confusing early hand wasting with motor neurone disease
Overlooking the shared GARS spectrum with CMT2D
Attributing pure motor weakness to a myopathy without electrophysiology
references: GeneReviews: GARS1-Associated Axonal Neuropathy and Distal Hereditary Motor Neuropathy
Bradley and Daroff's Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: No disease-modifying drug therapy exists; care centres on physiotherapy to maintain grip strength, dexterity and range of movement in the affected intrinsic hand muscles
Occupational therapy with hand splints, adaptive aids and assistive devices to support fine motor tasks lost to thenar and first dorsal interosseous wasting
Ankle-foot orthoses, podiatry and orthopaedic input for the foot deformity and foot drop that develop later
Regular neurological review to track progression of distal weakness and to detect and prevent hand contractures
Avoid neurotoxic drugs that could aggravate an axonal motor neuropathy
Multidisciplinary neuromuscular team input coordinating physiotherapy, orthotics and rehabilitation
Genetic counselling and predictive testing for at-risk relatives given autosomal dominant GARS or BSCL2 inheritance
